acabo: Acabar + gerund describes what someone ends up doing.
al: Al combines a and el. Al sol means in the sun.
aprendiéramos: After ojalá, the imperfect subjunctive expresses a wish that feels distant or uncertain.
Ojalá aprendiéramos algo nuevo cada día.
aquí: Aquí points to the place where the speaker is. Para tomar aquí means to have here.
banda: Banda sonora is the expression for a soundtrack.
Me encanta la banda sonora de esta película.
basta: Basta con + infinitive means all it takes is a particular action.
café: Café is masculine: un café. Café con leche is coffee with milk.
Tomo un café por la mañana.
con: Con connects things that go together, as in café con leche.
convierte: Convertirse en means to turn into or become something.
La conversación se convierte en una buena idea.
cuanto: Cuanto menos… más… means the less… the more… En cuanto means as soon as.
dedicaríamos: The conditional ending -íamos describes what we would do in a hypothetical situation.
dependiera: Si dependiera de mí means if it were up to me.
Si dependiera de mí, iríamos andando.
derecha: A la derecha means to the right.
La tienda está a la derecha.
desayuno: Here desayuno is a verb. As a noun, el desayuno means breakfast.
día: Ponerse al día means to catch up on news or recent events.
Tenemos mucho que contar para ponernos al día.
eso: Por eso means that is why.
Está lloviendo. Por eso llevo un paraguas.
está: Estar describes a current state or location.
falta: No hace falta means it is not necessary.
favor: Por favor is the polite expression please.
Un vaso de agua, por favor.
gira: Gira is an informal instruction to one person.
gusta: Me gusta means I like. Spanish literally frames the thing as pleasing to me.
Me gusta el café con leche.
hace: No hace falta que… means there is no need for something to happen.
No hace falta que vengas temprano.
hay: Hay works with singular and plural nouns.
Hay una mesa y dos sillas.
hemos: Hemos + past participle forms the present perfect: hemos salido, we have set out.
hola: A friendly everyday greeting that works at any time of day.
junto: Junto a means next to or beside.
El café está junto a la plaza.
leche: Leche is feminine: la leche. Con leche means with milk.
lleva: Here lleva is an informal instruction to bring something along.
llevar: Para llevar is the useful café phrase to go or takeaway.
Un café para llevar, por favor.
lo: Lo can turn an adjective into an idea: lo mejor means the best part.
me: In me gusta, me identifies the person who likes something.
merece: Merece la pena means it is worth it or worth the effort.
merecen: Merecen la pena is the plural form of the expression to be worth it.
mira: Mira is the informal command look, addressed to one person.
ojalá: Ojalá expresses a wish and is followed by the subjunctive.
para: Para introduces a purpose. Para tomar aquí means to have here.
Una mesa para dos, por favor.
pena: In merece la pena, pena is part of the expression to be worth the effort.
Vale la pena visitar este lugar.
pido: Pedir is used when ordering food or a drink.
Siempre pido un café con leche.
ponernos: Ponernos al día means for us to catch up.
Vamos a tomar algo y ponernos al día.
por: Por has several uses: por favor means please, and por esta calle means along this street.
quedamos: we meet; we arrange to meet
Quedar is a common way to talk about meeting friends.
quiero: Quiero can be used to order. Add por favor to make the request polite.
Quiero un vaso de agua, por favor.
se: Se is used with verbs such as convertirse, to become, and tratarse de, to be about.
El día se convierte en un recuerdo.
sea: Sea is the present subjunctive of ser, used here after aunque.
sigan: Seguir + gerund means to keep doing something. Sigan is a subjunctive form.
sonora: Banda sonora is the fixed expression for a soundtrack.
Esta película tiene una banda sonora preciosa.
sube: Sube is an informal instruction to go up.
temporada: Me gusta comprar fruta de temporada.
tengan: Tengan is the present subjunctive of tener, used here after no hace falta que.
No hace falta que tengan el mismo color.
terraza: In Spain, a terraza often means the outdoor seating area of a café or bar.
Vamos a sentarnos en la terraza.
tomar: Tomar is often used for having a drink or food. Para tomar aquí means to have here.
trata: Se trata de means it is about or it is a matter of.
Se trata de disfrutar del paseo.
tuviera: Como si is followed by the imperfect subjunctive to describe an imagined comparison.
Habla como si tuviera todo el tiempo del mundo.
vamos: Vamos a + infinitive can describe a plan or suggest doing something together.
veces: A veces camino hasta el trabajo.
vuelva: Vuelva is a subjunctive form of volver, used here after para que.
Guardo esta foto para que vuelva el recuerdo.
